strategies.name: Dispersion trading in equity indexes
strategies.desc: Sell index volatility and buy constituent volatility when index options imply more correlation than stocks actually deliver.
strategies.adapted_note: Uses realised constituent vols in place of single-stock implied vols (not on Yahoo Finance).

signal.label: DISPERSION ATTRACTIVE: index vol rich vs constituents

charts.title: Index volatility: India VIX vs constituent-implied theoretical

notes: PROXY: the book's trade is long ATM straddles on every constituent and short an index straddle (Eq. 423-424), which needs single-stock implied volatilities. Yahoo Finance has none for Indian stocks, so constituents' trailing 63-day realised volatilities stand in for their implied vols.
Index implied vol = India VIX. Implied correlation ρ = (σ²_VIX − Σw²σ²) / ((Σwσ)² − Σw²σ²). Weights: market-cap weights from Yahoo Finance.

Dispersion is attractive when the implied correlation sits well above what the constituents have actually realised (index options rich vs the basket). No P&L backtest is shown because it would need real option prices.

strategies.name: Dispersion trading – subset portfolio
strategies.desc: Run the dispersion trade on only the few constituents with the lowest idiosyncratic risk, using a PCA risk model to keep the correlation matrix stable.

signal.label: Trade 15-stock dispersion basket (12% of index weight)

tables.title: Subset: 15 stocks with the lowest specific-risk contribution w²σ²ξ²

notes: PROXY (see 6.3). The 252-day correlation matrix is replaced by a statistical risk model ψ = diag(ξ²) + Σₐ λₐ VₐVₐ' with K = 22 principal components (K from eRank = 21.8; Eqs. 425-427). The long straddle book only contains the 15 names with the smallest specific-risk term w²σ²ξ², which cuts the number of option legs while keeping the dispersion bet.
Index volatility implied by the risk model: 13.6% annualised vs India VIX 16.8%. Weights: market-cap weights from Yahoo Finance.

strategies.name: Index volatility targeting with risk-free asset
strategies.desc: Hold the index at a weight inversely proportional to its volatility so portfolio risk stays near a constant target, parking the rest in a risk-free asset.

notes: Risky weight w = σ*/σ with σ* = 12% and σ = India VIX (implied, forward-looking; used for the SENSEX too). Rest in a risk-free asset earning 6.5% (Yahoo Finance has no Indian T-bill series; this is an input in config.py). Max leverage 1.5x. Checked weekly; rebalanced only if the weight changes by more than 10% (the book's κ threshold).
